title: graceful-gh test regex matches any 2>/dev/null occurrence — passes even if degradation instruction is removed
description: Test in self-improve.test.mjs line 228: `assert.ok(/gh fails.*continue|failure.*never abort|2>/dev/null/i.test(code), 'graceful gh degradation missing')`. The regex has three alternatives joined by `|`. The third alternative `2>/dev/null` matches any shell error-redirect in the file. gig-cli.sh contains `2>/dev/null` in three unrelated places: the tmux `has-session` check on line 23 (status function), the has-session check on line 27 (restart case), and the `2>/dev/null` suffix on `gh issue list ... 2>/dev/null` and `gh issue create ... 2>/dev/null` in the cron prompt (line 21). As long as any one of these exists, the test passes. The actual graceful-degradation instruction ('If gh fails, log a warning and continue — gh failure must never abort the pass') could be deleted from the cron prompt and this test would still pass because `2>/dev/null` exists in unrelated lines. The test comment on line 227 ('The prompt says...') correctly identifies the TARGET phrase but the regex does not check for it.

additionalEvidence.note: Line 23 `2>/dev/null` is in the status() function — unrelated to gh graceful degradation. It alone satisfies the test's third alternative.

fix: Replace the regex with one that specifically targets the degradation instruction text in the cron prompt: `/gh fails.*log.*continue|If gh fails.*continue|gh failure.*never abort.*pass/i` with the `2>/dev/null` alternative removed. Or separately test that the cron prompt string contains both the `gh issue create` command AND the graceful-continue instruction in the same logical block.
